subject: Alpine Enterprise — request for executive clearance on warranty & indemnity redlines
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Alpine Enterprise — request for exec clearance on warranty & indemnity redlines

Hi Marissa / Ben —

Quick context: Alpine (prospect) is asking for a set of non-standard contract terms as part of a pilot agreement. ACV for year 1 is $225,000 (pilot + support), with potential to expand to enterprise-wide rollouts (upside in our pipeline ~ $1.2M ARR). They are asking for: a) removal of several warranty disclaimers; b) a broad (customer-friendly) indemnity that would cover claims not limited to IP or willful misconduct; and c) a liability cap set at "2x fees" (they believe that gives them comfort around data risk). They are also pressing for a one-time 35% discount to make the economics work for their procurement.

I attached their redlines (alpine_redlines_v3.docx) and our proposed MA plan (Alpine_MutualActionPlan.pdf). I need legal to confirm whether there is a path to accept any of these without creating unacceptable company exposure, and whether this requires executive (CEO/CRO/CFO) sign-off. If it does, please escalate and advise specific language that would mitigate risk.

Customer contacts: Ethan Cole (procurement), Lisa Park (legal). I copied Ben and Rishi for commercial context.

Ask: Marissa — can you review the redlines and indicate:
- whether we can accept mutual indemnity limited to IP and direct damages
- recommended maximum liability cap (absolute dollar number is preferred)
- whether warranty changes are acceptable with limited carve-ins (e.g., warranty limited to SLO breaches / reproducible defects only)

I think this is strategically important (pilot with potential roll-out), but I want to be explicit before we concede anything that could become policy precedent. If you recommend exec sign-off, please flag the approver and suggested language.

Thanks —
Mateo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Alpine Enterprise — request for exec clearance on warranty & indemnity redlines

Mateo — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I reviewed the redlines and flagged a few high-risk asks:

1) Indemnity: Alpine's proposed indemnity is very broad (covers third-party claims arising from customer data, and appears to remove limitations tied to IP or willful misconduct). That materially increases our exposure, especially if they claim consequential or third-party damages tied to data.

2) Liability cap: "2x fees" could be very large depending on multi-year extensions. Our standard cap is limited to fees paid in the prior 12 months; we sometimes make exceptions up to 2x fees for strategic deals, but prefer an absolute cap. I would recommend a maximum of $500,000 for this pilot (or 2x fees capped at $500k) if we must concede.

3) Warranty language: They want to carve out many of our disclaimers. We can entertain a limited warranty that covers reproducible defects and SLO failures with a remedies framework, but we should not expand to consequential damages or indemnify them for results of customer-provided data processing.

4) Security attestations: Alpine requires SOC 2 + SSO (SAML). Those are fine but must be captured in the SOW and security appendix; they do not replace indemnity/liability considerations.

Commercial trade-offs: I understand the 35% ask is aimed at closing the pilot. If you can reduce the discount to 25–30% and secure a firm expansion commitment (MOU in writing / kickoff within 90 days upon pilot success), that weakens the argument for broad indemnity.

Recommendation: If the customer insists on (A) a broad indemnity or (B) a liability cap higher than $500k, we should escalate to execs for sign-off. Suggested exec approver chain: Vivek Kulkarni (CRO) for commercial concession + Vivek to loop in CFO if they push beyond $500k. If you want me to draft counter-language, I can — but I'll need the final commercial position (discount %, cap tolerance).

LMK within the hour if you want me to prepare a redline that limits indemnity to IP/willful misconduct and sets the cap at $500k.

—Marissa
Chief Legal Officer (acting) — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Alpine Enterprise — request for exec clearance on warranty & indemnity redlines

Marissa — appreciate the rapid read. Quoting a few lines from Ethan (Alpine procurement) to show their urgency:

> "We need the vendor to accept broader indemnity for data-related claims — we cannot sign with limited carveouts. Also, procurement needs a liability posture aligned to 2x fees to cover our internal risk models. Without these, we can't get procurement committee approval."

Commercial context: Alpine is running a pilot at two business units, and if it converts they plan to deploy Redwood across ~400 seats. The seller promise is that successful pilot + case study unlocks larger procurement approvals. That is why they're asking for more vendor-friendly terms.

Counter-proposal I'm willing to push to the customer if legal approves:
- Mutual indemnity limited to IP infringement and willful misconduct (no broad data indemnity).
- Liability cap of $500,000 absolute (explicitly 2x fees capped at $500k if they insist on formula semantics).
- One-time discount: 30% for year 1 (instead of 35% requested).
- Acceptance of SOC2 + SAML requirements in SOW.

If legal can sign off on the above, I will present it as a final compromise. If legal requires the company to escalate for any of the three points above (broad indemnity, cap > $500k, or open-ended warranty carveouts), please escalate to Vivek per Marissa's note.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/DEAL-2028-0142

Thanks —
Mateo

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Alpine Enterprise — executive approval requested (warranty/indemnity/liability cap + one-time discount)

Vivek — short summary and ask.

Summary:
- Account: Alpine Enterprise (pilot, potential $1.2M ARR if expanded).
- Current ACV (pilot): $225,000 (year 1).
- Customer asks: broad indemnity covering data claims, removal of warranty disclaimers, liability cap = "2x fees", and 35% discount.
- Legal assessment (Marissa): broad indemnity and cap > $500k are high risk. Recommend limiting indemnity to IP and willful misconduct; set maximum cap at $500k for this pilot.
- Commercial: Customer wants stronger vendor protections; they will only approve procurement with those concessions. Our compromise ask to customer (pending your approval): mutual indemnity limited to IP + willful misconduct, absolute liability cap $500k, one-time 30% discount, SOC2 attestation and SAML in SOW, written expansion commitment (MOU) tied to pilot success.

Why I recommend approving an exception:
- Strategic upside: high probability of multi-product expansion if pilot succeeds; we would secure a strong reference in their industry.
- Economics: even with 30% discount, the year-1 revenue plus expansion potential makes this a high-leverage win.
- Mitigations: require SOC2 + security appendix, narrow indemnity language to specific categories, timebox the liability exposure to the pilot term, and require a signed MOU committing to a post-pilot rollout discussion.

Decision requested (please reply with Approve / Decline):
1) Approve mutual indemnity limited to IP and willful misconduct?
2) Approve liability cap of $500,000 for this pilot (company exception)?
3) Approve one-time 30% discount for year 1 contingent on MOU for expansion?

If you approve, Marissa will finalize the redline language and I will present as the final commercial offer to Alpine. If you decline, please indicate which items to push back on so I can negotiate downward.

Attachments: alpine_redlines_v3.docx, Alpine_MutualActionPlan.pdf
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/deal/DEAL-2028-0142

Thanks for the quick read —
